cards.explanation: The answer is a sign from heaven. The Pharisees and Sadducees come and test Jesus by asking Him to show them a sign from heaven (Matthew 16:1). Notice they aren't just asking. The text says they came to test Him. I think that's a very different way to knock on a door, friends.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says that in the morning they say, “Today it will be stormy, for the sky is red and overcast.” (Matthew 16:3). Red sky at night, fair weather. Red and overcast in the morning, storm. They read the sky like someone who glances at the clouds and grabs an umbrella before the first drop.

The answer is the signs of the times. Jesus says, “You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky, but not the signs of the times.” (Matthew 16:3). They could read clouds like a pro, friends. The bigger signs were right in front of them, and they didn't read those.

The answer is Jonah, friends. Jesus says none will be given “…except the sign of Jonah.” (Matthew 16:4). Jonah was a prophet who ran from God's call to go to Nineveh (Jonah 1:1-3). Jesus doesn't spell out the sign in this passage, so I'll leave it right there.
The answer is False, friends. Jesus doesn't stay to keep debating. Matthew 16:4 says, “Then He left them and went away.” No debate club, no second round. He says what He says and goes.
The answer is bread, friends. Matthew 16:5 says the disciples forgot to take bread. Now, I've forgotten the baking powder before, and I live in a bakery. It happens to the best of us.

The answer is True, friends. The disciples discuss it among themselves and conclude, “It is because we did not bring any bread.” (Matthew 16:7). Jesus says leaven, and their minds go straight to the bread basket. I think we've all heard one word and run the wrong direction with it.
The answer is True, friends. The text says Jesus was “Aware of their conversation…” (Matthew 16:8). They were talking among themselves, and He knew what they were saying. Then He speaks up.

The answer is loaves, friends! Jesus asks, “Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand…?” and then “Or the seven loaves for the four thousand…” (Matthew 16:9-10). He asks how many basketfuls they gathered each time. He brings up those loaves right when they're debating having no bread (Matthew 16:8).

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says, “How do you not understand that I was not telling you about bread?” (Matthew 16:11). Plain as day, and they'd missed it. I once stamped a whole batch upside down, so I won't throw stones.

The answer is teaching, friends. Matthew 16:12 says they understood He was not telling them to beware of the leaven used in bread, “…but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” Leaven is something I know from my bakery, and I never once thought of it as teaching. Jesus did.
